newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Cargo-Passenger links can be different - Lufthansa.
newsitem.headline: Cargo-Passenger links can be different - Lufthansa.

text.p: German airline Lufthansa said on Tuesday that transport needs could make it necessary for airlines to develop different cargo and passenger partnerships.

"You are not necessarily going to have the same partner on cargo as you do for passengers," Lufthansa Cargo Northern Europe Marketing Manager Lars Gurfeldt told an air cargo conference in this western Swedish city.

Lufthansa owns 25 percent of Luxembourg-based cargo carrier Cargolux and 25 percent of DHL. Gurfeldt said passenger and cargo divisions of airlines often developed along separate commercial routes which demanded different partnerships.
Lufthansa's cargo division cooperated closely with Singpore Airlines while the passanger division was in hot cometition with the Asian carrier, he added.

Lufthansa Northern Europe Cargo director Martin Schlingensiepen told Reuters attitudes were changing towards cargo, with airlines changing their views on charging for belly capacity, which they had virtually given away in the past.
He said cargo had often been regarded as a by-product of passenger traffic in the past but cargo's profitability now made that an outdated notion.
"Most airlines finally realise there is money to be made in cargo," he added.

Both officials said the cargo divisions of airlines were bound to expand as freight volumes increase sharply, but there were no signs that airlines would split their operations into separate listed entities.
"The focus will simply fall more and more on cargo operations," Schlingensiepen said.
